---
title: "Use the Spinorama Python library"
date: 2026-08-22
abstract: >
  Load loudspeaker measurements, compute Spinorama curves and preference scores,
  and create plots with Python.
---

This page is a compact Python tutorial for working with one measurement set.
Run it from the repository root with the virtual environment and
`PYTHONPATH=src` configured as described in [Install and run Spinorama](02_install.qmd).
The examples are illustrative; code execution is disabled for the manual
project.

## Load a text measurement set

The generic horizontal/vertical text loader expects files for the measured
angles. A complete set normally contains 72 files: horizontal and vertical
measurements at 10-degree increments from -170 to 180 degrees.

```{python}
from spinorama.constant_paths import DEFAULT_FREQ_RANGE, MEAN_MAX, MEAN_MIN
from spinorama.load import filter_graphs
from spinorama.loaders.spl_hv_txt import parse_graph_spl_hv_txt

speaker = "Ascend Acoustics Sierra-2EX V2"
directory = f"datas/measurements/{speaker}/vendor"

_, spl_h = parse_graph_spl_hv_txt(directory, "H")
_, spl_v = parse_graph_spl_hv_txt(directory, "V")

measurements = filter_graphs(
    speaker,
    spl_h,
    spl_v,
    MEAN_MIN,
    MEAN_MAX,
    mformat="spl_hv_txt",
    mdistance=1.0,
)
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Version 2.0 import paths"}
Version 2.0 removes the legacy flat modules. Replace `spinorama.load_*` with
`spinorama.loaders.*`, `spinorama.compute_*` with `spinorama.compute.*`,
`spinorama.filter_*` with `spinorama.filters.*`, and `spinorama.extract_*`
with `spinorama.extract.*`.
:::

## Compute Spinorama curves

```{python}
from spinorama.compute.cea2034 import compute_cea2034, estimated_inroom_hv

spin = compute_cea2034(
    measurements.h_spl,
    measurements.v_spl,
)
pir = estimated_inroom_hv(
    measurements.h_spl,
    measurements.v_spl,
)
```

The resulting data include the on-axis response, listening window, early
reflections, sound power, directivity indices, and predicted in-room response.
The exact fields available depend on the input format and completeness of the
measurement set.

## Compute preference scores

```{python}
from spinorama.compute.scores import speaker_pref_rating
from spinorama.misc import graph_melt

scores = speaker_pref_rating(
    graph_melt(spin),
    graph_melt(pir),
    rounded=True,
)
scores
```

Scores are derived from the measurement data and are not a substitute for
listening, room evaluation, distortion measurements, or maximum-output data.
Compare measurements of similar quality and processing before comparing
scores.

## Plot the results

The on-axis phase plot defaults to wrapping phase into −180° to 180° after
removing a delay estimated from the linear phase slope between 12 and 16 kHz.
The axis title shows the estimated delay. If fewer than three valid samples
are available in that band, the measured delay is retained and the title says
so. This changes the plot only; the measurement data are not changed.

On the website, the On Axis plot offers **Wrap phase** and **Remove delay**
checkboxes. The same settings are available in the plot options menu and
apply to On Axis plots in speaker, comparison, and similar-speaker views.
Graphs must be regenerated to include the phase data needed by these controls.

For Python callers, pass `phase_wrap=False` or `phase_remove_delay=False`
in the plot parameters to change either behavior. These options are also
accepted by `build_figures` in its parameters dictionary. When phase is
already wrapped, unwrapping assumes adjacent samples differ by less than
180°; large delays or sparse samples can make the estimate ambiguous.

```{python}
import spinorama.plot as plot

plot_params = plot.plot_params_default.copy()
plot_params.update(width=800, height=500, layout="compact")

figure = plot.plot_spinorama(
    spin=spin,
    params=plot_params,
    minmax_slopes=None,
    is_normalized=False,
    valid_freq_range=DEFAULT_FREQ_RANGE,
)
figure
```

Other plot helpers include:

- `plot.plot_graph` for a single response;
- `plot.plot_graph_flat` for a response with regression lines;
- `plot.plot_graph_regression` for the predicted in-room response;
- `plot.plot_contour` and `plot.plot_contour_3d` for directivity; and
- `plot.plot_radar` for polar directivity views.

For a ready-made command-line workflow that loads all supported formats and
writes PNG and JSON files, use [Compute a Spinorama](08_compute_spin.qmd).
